title: The Black Panther Party
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history of the Black Panther Party, from its founding in Oakland by Huey Newton and Bobby Seal and its Ten Point Program, through armed patrols of police, community survival programs like the free breakfast and Oakland Community School, the FBI's COINTELPRO campaign against it, the killing of Fred Hampton, internal splits with Eldridge Cleaver, the Alex Rackley case, Bobby Seal's mayoral run, and the group's legacy. The episode closes with a listener mail about the rubber trade in Latin America.

segments.title: Technical glitch notice and opening banter
segments.summary: Josh notes minor audio glitches in the episode, then introduces the Black Panther Party topic as a history neither host learned much about in school.

segments.title: Context: Jim Crow era and early militancy
segments.summary: The hosts describe the racial conditions of the Jim Crow and New Deal era, Robert Williams' book Negroes with Guns, and how Huey Newton and Bobby Seal formed the Black Panther Party for Self Defense in Oakland in 1966, citing the panther metaphor.
topics: Black Panther Party for Self Defense

segments.title: Influences: Malcolm X, Marxism and class struggle
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the party differed from Martin Luther King Jr.'s nonviolent approach, the influence of Malcolm X, willingness to work with other groups regardless of race, and the party's Marxist view that capitalism was the core problem.

segments.title: The Ten Point Program
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read the party's Ten Point Program covering freedom, full employment, housing, education, military exemption, police brutality, prisoner release, trials by peers, and a UN-supervised plebiscite. The program was printed and distributed, and the party's newspaper The Black Panther ran it on the inside cover.

segments.title: Branding, membership growth and police patrols
segments.summary: The hosts describe the party's black leather and beret look, the Black Is Beautiful movement, rapid growth to about five thousand members, and armed patrols that monitored police traffic stops in Oakland, along with the California open carry loophole that Eldridge Cleaver identified and the resulting 1967 legislative response Reagan backed.

segments.title: Women in the party and Eldridge Cleaver
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Eldridge Cleaver as minister of information and author of Soul on Ice, the roles of Kathleen Cleaver and Elaine Brown, and the party's male-dominated leadership despite many women in rank and file roles.

segments.title: Survival programs and Oakland Community School
segments.summary: The party's survival programs included free breakfasts for children, free medical clinics, and the Oakland Community School run by Elaine Brown. The hosts note the programs' community support and Hoover's concern that these programs would win outside support.

segments.title: COINTELPRO, Hoover, and the Fred Hampton raid
segments.summary: The hosts explain the FBI's COINTELPRO campaign against the party, Hoover's view that the breakfast programs were a threat, Huey Newton's imprisonment and the Free Huey campaign, and the December 1969 Chicago police raid that killed Fred Hampton and Mark Clark, which used an FBI informant's map.

segments.title: Internal splits, Black Liberation Army and Alex Rackley case
segments.summary: The hosts cover the Newton and Cleaver factional split, the Black Liberation Army's turn to violence, Newton's drug addiction, the 1969 Alex Rackley murder in New Haven and Bobby Seal's trial, and the loss of public sympathy.

segments.title: Bobby Seal's mayoral run, Chicago Eight and Panther 21
segments.summary: The hosts describe Bobby Seal's run for Oakland mayor and its loss in a runoff, Seal's contempt sentence in the Chicago Eight trial, the Panther 21 conspiracy trial in New York, and the Hillary Clinton urban legend about the Rackley case.

segments.title: Legacy, lynching statistics and Black Lives Matter
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the party's cultural legacy, Eldridge Cleaver's later view tying gang violence to the party's destruction, Tuskegee lynching records, 2015 police killings, and comparisons to Black Lives Matter. They close with recommended resources and a film discussion.

segments.title: Listener mail: rubber trade addendum
segments.summary: A listener writes to add that the Peruvian Amazon and Putumayo region were major rubber sites, describing Julio Cesar Arana's Casa Arana atrocities against indigenous people.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and give contact and website information.
